The headers of one part must fit in 1024 bytes, and a part whose headers run past that raises `MultiPartParserError` (`django/http/multipartparser.py:parse_boundary_stream`).

Otherwise fields go to `POST` and files to the handlers, and at the end the handlers are told through `FileUploadHandler.upload_complete`, until one returns a true value (`django/http/multipartparser.py:MultiPartParser._parse`).

The body is no larger than `settings.FILE_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE`, so `MemoryFileUploadHandler.handle_raw_input` sets the handler's `activated` flag, which has it keep the request's files in memory ([Upload handlers and uploaded files](uploads.md#memory-or-disk)) (`django/core/files/uploadhandler.py:MemoryFileUploadHandler.handle_raw_input`).

A file is known to be complete only when the next part begins, so `handle_file_complete` runs at the top of the next turn of the loop, and the first handler whose `FileUploadHandler.file_complete` returns a file makes the entry in `FILES` (`django/http/multipartparser.py:MultiPartParser._parse`, `django/http/multipartparser.py:MultiPartParser.handle_file_complete`).

A request that fails raises `MultiPartParserError`, which becomes a 400 response ([How an exception becomes a response](../handlers/exceptions.md)) (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:response_for_exception`).
The method also settles the chunk size: the smallest `FileUploadHandler.chunk_size` among the handlers, 64 KB for the two Django installs (`django/http/multipartparser.py:MultiPartParser.__init__`).

Otherwise the parser does not hold the body to the number: under WSGI the request's `LimitedStream` stops the body at the declared length, and under ASGI nothing does, so the parser reads the body's file to its end ([The body: `body`, `POST` and `FILES`](body.md)) (`django/http/multipartparser.py:MultiPartParser._parse`, `django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:LimitedStream`).

No next part begins, so the file is never completed: the handlers are told through `FileUploadHandler.upload_interrupted`, the file is dropped, and the view sees the fields that came before it (`django/http/multipartparser.py:MultiPartParser._parse`).

A file input that was left empty still sends a part, with an empty file name, and `parse_boundary_stream` classes it as a field: the input's name turns up in `POST` with an empty value (`django/http/multipartparser.py:MultiPartParser._parse`, `django/http/multipartparser.py:parse_boundary_stream`).

When it is left with an empty name, `"."` or `".."`, it returns `None`, and the parser goes on without reading the rest of the part: a three-byte file sent with the file name `"../"` between two fields leaves both fields in `POST` and nothing of itself in `POST` or `FILES` (`django/http/multipartparser.py:MultiPartParser.sanitize_file_name`, `django/http/multipartparser.py:MultiPartParser._parse`).
